Swings","printedPage":478,"additionalStudyPoints":[],"sourceBodyWords":160,"addedWords":0,"sourceParagraphs":4}],"masterclassCount":1},{"id":"bp14-m14-3","chapterId":"bp14-ch14","moduleId":"bp14-m14-3","moduleNumber":"14.3","title":"Schizophrenia","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":481,"printedEnd":491,"pdfStart":499,"pdfEnd":509,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Schizophrenia involves multiple symptom dimensions and requires careful differential diagnosis. Genetic vulnerability interacts with developmental and environmental factors, and researchers continue to examine brain and neurotransmitter changes."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module reviews dopamine-related antipsychotic treatments and newer approaches, including interest in glutamate. Keep positive symptoms, negative symptoms, cognitive difficulties, and treatment limitations distinct."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-3-study-1","text":"What schizophrenia means"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Schizophrenia is associated with disturbances in perception, beliefs, thinking, motivation, and social or occupational functioning. The term does not mean multiple personalities. Positive symptoms refer to experiences or behaviors added to typical functioning, such as hallucinations or delusions; negative symptoms refer to reductions in functions such as motivation or expressive behavior. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment and consideration of other possible causes. Biological measures are informative for research but are not simple stand-alone diagnostic tests."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-3-study-2","text":"Genetic susceptibility and environment"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Family and adoption research supports a genetic contribution to risk, but schizophrenia does not follow one straightforward Mendelian pattern. Many genetic variants and developmental influences are implicated, and having a predisposition does not mean the disorder will necessarily develop. Research considers prenatal and early-life factors, later stressors, and other environmental influences. Findings from group studies need careful interpretation because different people may arrive at similar clinical symptoms through partly different pathways."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-3-study-3","text":"Brain findings and explanatory limits"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Studies report differences in certain brain structures, circuits, and aspects of neural function among groups, but these findings overlap with variation in the wider population. A structural difference does not by itself establish whether it contributed to the disorder, followed from illness, or relates to treatment or other factors. Researchers therefore combine anatomical, behavioral, and pharmacological evidence rather than claiming to have discovered one unique 'schizophrenia region'."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-3-study-4","text":"Dopamine, glutamate, and treatment"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many antipsychotic drugs influence dopamine receptors and can reduce particular symptoms, supporting a role for dopamine-related pathways. However, the dopamine account does not explain all features of schizophrenia. Glutamate-related processes and other signaling systems have also received attention. Newer treatments may differ in receptor action and adverse effects, but medication alone does not address every functional difficulty. A complete view includes symptom management, psychological and social support, and the limits of current mechanistic understanding."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h01","text":"Diagnosis"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although the term is Greek for split mind , it does not mean an alternation among personalities.","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"What Bleuler meant by schizophrenia was a split between the emotional and intellectual aspects of experience: Someone might giggle or cry for no apparent reason or react inappropriately to good or bad news.","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Detachment of emotion from intellect is no longer considered a central feature of schizophrenia, but the term lives on.","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because schizophrenia often produces long-term debilitation with onset in young adulthood, it is a major health problem in terms of the loss of productive, enjoyable years of life.","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although the first diagnosis of schizophrenia usually occurs in early adulthood, mild problems usually begin in childhood, including deficits in attention, memory, and impulse control .","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to DSM-5 , the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, 5th edition , to be diagnosed with schizophrenia, someone must have deteriorated in everyday functioning (work, interpersonal relations, self-care) for at least 6 months for reasons not","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The genetics vary among people diagnosed with schizophrenia, and so do the brain abnormalities.","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although DSM-5 does not list cognitive symptoms as essential to the diagnosis, cognitive impairments are common in schizophrenia.","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cognitive impairments correlate with lower-than-average heart rate variability, which implies abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system .","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition to the defining symptoms, researchers have reported unexplained oddities that are characteristic of many people with schizophrenia:","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h02","text":"Differential Diagnosis of Schizophrenia"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even if someone’s symptoms clearly match the description of schizophrenia, a therapist must make a differential diagnosis —that is, one that rules out other","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Here are a few conditions that sometimes resemble schizophrenia:","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h03","text":"Genetic Influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Examining chromosome 4 can reveal with almost perfect accuracy whether someone will or will not develop the disease.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although schizophrenia and other psychiatric disorders have high heritability, they do not depend on any single gene.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h04","text":"Family Studies"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One of the most important points in Figure 14.13 is that monozygotic twins have a higher concordance (agreement) for schizophrenia than do dizygotic twins.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Furthermore, twin pairs who are monozygotic but thought they weren’t, are more concordant than twin pairs who thought they were, but really aren’t .","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The high concordance for monozygotic twins has long been taken as strong evidence for a genetic influence.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, note that monozygotic twins have only about 50 percent concordance, and some studies show even less .","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Also note the greater similarity between dizygotic twins than between siblings in Figure 14.13.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dizygotic twins have the same genetic resemblance as siblings but greater environmental similarity, including prenatal environment.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h05","text":"Adopted Children Who Develop Schizophrenia"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For adopted children who develop schizophrenia, the disorder is more common in their biological relatives than their adopting relatives.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A Danish study found schizophrenia in 12.5 percent of the immediate biological relatives and none of the adopting relatives .","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Note in Figure 14.13 that children of a mother with schizophrenia have a moderately high probability of schizophrenia, even if adopted by mentally healthy parents.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The adoption results suggest a genetic basis, but they are also consistent with a prenatal influence.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When their children develop schizophrenia, we cannot be sure that the reason is genetic.","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A study of adopted children in Finland found a high probability of schizophrenia or related conditions among","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"children who had a biological mother with schizophrenia and a severely disordered adopting family.","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h06","text":"Identified Genes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers working with various populations have identified hundreds of genetic loci that differ on average between people with or without schizophrenia, including many that code for proteins in the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The results vary from one study to another, partly because some genes are common in one ethnic group but not in another .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"No common genetic variant produces more than a small increase in the probability of schizophrenia.","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A few rare genes are known to greatly increase the risk of schizophrenia, mostly by disrupting the development of glutamate synapses or by interfering with the immune system .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Certain genes are described as “intolerant of loss of function.” Geneticists only occasionally find variants in those genes because the variants decrease survival or reproduction.","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The common genes producing a small risk and the rare genes causing a greater risk mostly affect the same brain functions, just to different degrees .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even a tiny deletion of a critical segment can lead to cognitive dysfunction and symptoms of schizophrenia .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h07","text":"Environmental Influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to the neurodevelopmental hypothesis , prenatal or neonatal difficulties—of either genetic or environmental origin—can produce abnormalities in the developing brain that predispose to schizophrenia .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, an area often impaired in schizophrenia, is one of the slowest brain areas to mature.","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When researchers damaged it in infants, the monkeys’ behavior was nearly normal at age 1 year, but worse at age 2 years .","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Presumably, the effects of brain damage were minimal at age 1 year because the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex doesn’t do much at that age anyway.","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Later, when it should begin assuming important functions, the damage makes a difference (Figure 14.15).","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h08","text":"Prenatal or Early Postnatal Factors"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The risk of schizophrenia is mildly elevated among people who had problems that could affect early brain development, including poor prenatal nutrition, premature birth, low birth","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Related evidence comes from the season-of-birth effect , the tendency for people born in winter to have a slightly increased probability of developing schizophrenia.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Therefore, the reasoning goes, many pregnant women become infected in the fall with a virus that impairs a crucial stage of brain development in a baby who will be born in the winter or early spring.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers retrieved blood samples that hospitals had taken from pregnant women and stored for decades.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The mother’s infection also causes a fever, which slows the division of fetal neurons . (Exercise during pregnancy does not overheat the abdomen and is not dangerous to the fetus.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hot baths and saunas pose a possible risk, however.) A prenatal immune reaction can also activate microglia that impair mitochondria and synapse formation .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h09","text":"Factors Later in Life"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physical, emotional, or sexual abuse during childhood increases the risk and the probable severity of later schizophrenia .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Traumatic experiences early in life impair the ability of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis to produce its usual negative feedback relationship.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The effect is exaggerated in people with a genetic predisposition to a strong stress reaction .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Urban environments are associated with decreased sunlight, increased air pollution, and other factors that might contribute to vulnerability, but it is also possible that people at risk of schizophrenia tend to move to big cities .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This parasite reproduces only in cats, but people can be exposed to it by handling infected cats, by playing in soil or sand where cats have defecated, or by eating chicken or pork after those animals were fed in infected soil.","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parasite does not always cross into the human brain, but if it does, it impairs a child’s brain development .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h10","text":"Brain Abnormalities"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people with schizophrenia show mild abnormalities of brain anatomy, including less-than-average gray matter in the frontal cortex, hippocampus, and other areas .","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"White matter is reduced also, and the ventricles (fluid-filled spaces within the brain) are enlarged (Kochunov and Hong, 2014;","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the brain abnormalities are highly variable, and mild in most cases .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of the brain abnormalities are present at the time of first diagnosis, with only slight deterioration after the first few years .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even when further deterioration does occur, it could be a result of drug abuse (common in people with schizophrenia) rather than a result of schizophrenia itself .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An example of a task that tests for damage to the prefrontal cortex is the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test.","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with damage to the prefrontal cortex have no trouble following whichever rule comes first, but they have trouble shifting to a new rule.","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h11","text":"Treatments"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Before antipsychotic drugs became available in the mid- 1950s, most people with schizophrenia were indefinitely confined to mental hospitals.","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Today, effective drugs and outpatient treatment offer more hope.","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h12","text":"Antipsychotic Drugs and Dopamine"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"With long-term use, the side effects increase, and the effectiveness against schizophrenia often decreases .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For each drug, researchers determined the mean dose prescribed for patients with schizophrenia (displayed along the horizontal axis) and the amount needed to block dopamine receptors (displayed along the vertical axis).","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As Figure 14.17 shows, the drugs that are most effective against schizophrenia (and therefore used in the smallest doses) are the most effective at blocking dopamine receptors .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That finding inspired the dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia , which holds that schizophrenia results from excess activity at dopamine synapses in certain brain areas.","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although the concentration of dopamine in the brain is no higher than normal, dopamine release is increased in the basal ganglia, especially in response to stressful events .","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"that abuse of amphetamine, methamphetamine, or cocaine (which all increase dopamine at the synapses) can induce substance-induced psychotic disorder , characterized by hallucinations and delusions.","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because IBZM binds only to receptors that dopamine did not already bind, measuring the radioactivity counts the number of vacant dopamine receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because AMPT had prevented production of dopamine, all D 2 receptors should be vacant at this time, so the researchers got a count of the total.","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h13","text":"Newer Antipsychotic Drugs"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Drugs that block dopamine synapses produce their benefits by acting on neurons in the mesolimbocortical system , neurons that project from the midbrain to the limbic system and prefrontal cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, these drugs also block dopamine neurons in the mesostriatal system that projects to the basal ganglia, and in doing so they produce tardive dyskinesia (TARD-eev dis-kih-NEE-zhee-uh), characterized by tremors and other involuntary movements .","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Compared to drugs like haloperidol, the second-generation antipsychotics have less effect on dopamine receptors, but they also increase the release of glutamate .","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Third-generation antipsychotic drugs, which act mainly at dopamine type 2 receptors, avoid both the movement problems and the weight gain .","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An interesting point emerges from studies comparing one antipsychotic drug against another: In 90 percent of the studies that were sponsored by a drug company, the results favored the drug sold by the sponsoring company .","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h14","text":"Role of Glutamate"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to the glutamate hypothesis of schizophrenia , schizophrenia results at least in part from a dysfunction of glutamate transmission.","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The original evidence for this hypothesis was that phencyclidine (PCP) and ketamine, which antagonize NMDA-type glutamate receptors, produce effects resembling both the positive and negative symptoms of schizophrenia.","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They also induce a relapse for someone who has recovered from schizophrenia. .","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Chronic ketamine use causes a loss of gray matter in several brain areas, similar to the pattern sometimes seen in patients with schizophrenia .","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ordinarily, those NMDA receptors stimulate neurons that inhibit other cells from releasing glutamate, but because the NMDA receptors have reduced activity, the result is excessive release of glutamate in other places, contributing to symptoms of the disorder.","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a result of the complexity, drugs that affect glutamate release might or might not be helpful, depending on the stage of the disease and other factors.","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-3-h15","text":"In Closing: Many Remaining Mysteries"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In most areas of medicine, treatment today is far more successful than in past decades.","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, in psychopathology, and particularly in schizophrenia, research has led to improved understanding without much improvement in patients’ outcome .","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One reason is that many patients do not get the treatments that are available, or do not get it early enough.","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research is a little like reading a good mystery novel that presents a mixture of important clues and irrelevant information.","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In research on schizophrenia, we have much information, but also gaps and points that don’t seem to fit.","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, over the last several decades, the use of marijuana has increased while the prevalence of schizophrenia has not.","sourcePrintedPage":490,"sourcePdfPage":508,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"The best estimate is that about 7 to 8 people per 1,000 will develop schizophrenia at some point in life.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499},{"type":"bullet","text":"It occurs in all ethnic groups and all parts of the world, but in some countries more than others, and somewhat more often in men than in women.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":481,"sourcePdfPage":499},{"type":"bullet","text":"Many healthy people have occasionally heard a voice when they knew they were alone.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500},{"type":"bullet","text":"The first four items on the list—delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and disorganized behavior— are called positive symptoms, meaning behaviors that are present that should be absent.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500},{"type":"bullet","text":"Whenever it is the same as the last letter that you attended to, you should press a key.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500},{"type":"bullet","text":"Most people’s speech becomes less clear when they perform this memory task while trying to tell a story.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500},{"type":"bullet","text":"If it is the second presentation of a picture, requiring them to avoid what they said the first time and tell a totally new story, the memory task causes even greater interference, and speech becomes incoherent, much like schizophrenic speech.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":482,"sourcePdfPage":500},{"type":"bullet","text":"The more closely you are biologically related to someone with schizophrenia, the greater your own probability of schizophrenia, as shown in Figure 14.13.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"That is, being monozygotic is more important than being treated as monozygotic.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"A pregnant woman with schizophrenia passes her genes to her child, but she also provides the prenatal environment.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"Many women with schizophrenia abuse alcohol or other drugs, eat a poor diet, and have complications during pregnancy and delivery.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"The genetic risk itself or the disordered family itself had less effect, as shown in Figure 14.14.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"Indeed, it would be difficult for any gene with a strong link to schizophrenia to become common, because people with schizophrenia have, on average, fewer than half as many children as other people do, and their brothers and sisters do not compensate by having more children than average.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"One common gene related to schizophrenia alters the major histocompatibility complex—that is, genes controlling cell surface proteins that the immune system recognizes.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another important gene, called DISC1 (disrupted in schizophrenia 1), controls differentiation and migration of neurons in brain development, production of dendritic spines, the generation of new neurons in the hippocampus, and learning.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"Brain abnormalities occurring in infancy might not show their full effects until later.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another way to explain the relationship between early impairment and later symptoms is the two-hit hypothesis.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to this proposal, schizophrenia is the result of a combination of a genetic predisposition and impacts from the environment in prenatal/neonatal development, later in life, or both.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"The risk also increases if the mother was exposed to extreme stress, such as the sudden death of a close relative, early in her pregnancy or if the mother had almost any prolonged illness during pregnancy.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"They found increased incidence of influenza virus among mothers whose children eventually developed schizophrenia.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"Each of these early factors correlates only slightly with schizophrenia.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"By themselves, none has a big effect, but they can combine with genetics or later insults.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"As a result, any stress reaction later in life is prolonged.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"The incidence of schizophrenia is also elevated among people who immigrate from one country to another.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":485,"sourcePdfPage":503},{"type":"bullet","text":"As you might predict, people with schizophrenia perform poorly at tasks that depend on the prefrontal cortex.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504},{"type":"bullet","text":"Suppose someone hands you a shuffled deck of cards that differ in number, color, and shape of objects—for example, the first three cards might show two red circles, five blue triangles, and four green squares.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504},{"type":"bullet","text":"Other antipsychotic, or neuroleptic, drugs (drugs that tend to relieve schizophrenia and similar conditions) occur in two chemical families: the phenothiazines (FEE-no-THI-uh-zeens), which include chlorpromazine, and the butyrophenones (BYOO-tir-oh- FEE-noans), which include haloperidol (trade name Haldol).","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h12","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504},{"type":"bullet","text":"Behavioral benefits of any of these drugs develop gradually over weeks, as the drug gradually accumulates in the synapses.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h12","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504},{"type":"bullet","text":"In a clever study, researchers measured the number of dopamine receptors occupied at a given moment.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h12","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505},{"type":"bullet","text":"Drugs called second-generation antipsychotics, or atypical antipsychotics, relieve schizophrenic symptoms with less risk of movement problems.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h13","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"The most common of these drugs are clozapine and risperidone.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h13","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"Studies have disagreed about whether the second-generation antipsychotics improve quality of life more than the original drugs do.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h13","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"It is possible to bias a study in subtle ways, by altering the doses of two drugs, choosing patients who seem likely to respond to the sponsor’s drug, or choosing one measurement instead of another to report.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h13","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers do not have a consensus about the role of glutamate, but here is one somewhat complicated version: A tendency toward schizophrenia begins with reduced activity of NMDA receptors in the hippocampus, caused by a combination of genetic and environmental forces.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h14","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"Excessive glutamate release can overstimulate neurons and thereby kill them and, after prolonged illness, even if someone has recovered from the positive symptoms, many neurons in the cortex may have died, causing negative and cognitive symptoms.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h14","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506},{"type":"bullet","text":"Yes, I told you it was going to be complicated.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h14","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another is that our understanding of the condition, though improved, is still far from complete.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h15","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507},{"type":"bullet","text":"It will be fascinating to see what develops in future research.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h15","sourcePrintedPage":489,"sourcePdfPage":507},{"type":"bullet","text":"On average, people who use much marijuana are more likely than others to develop schizophrenia.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h15","sourcePrintedPage":490,"sourcePdfPage":508},{"type":"bullet","text":"One of the most important points in Figure 14.13 is that monozygotic twins have a higher concordance (agreement) for schizophrenia than do dizygotic twins.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"For adopted children who develop schizophrenia, the disorder is more common in their biological relatives than their adopting relatives.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":483,"sourcePdfPage":501},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers working with various populations have identified hundreds of genetic loci that differ on average between people with or without schizophrenia, including many that code for proteins in the brain .","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":484,"sourcePdfPage":502},{"type":"bullet","text":"With long-term use, the side effects increase, and the effectiveness against schizophrenia often decreases .","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","sourcePrintedPage":486,"sourcePdfPage":504},{"type":"bullet","text":"Drugs that block dopamine synapses produce their benefits by acting on neurons in the mesolimbocortical system , neurons that project from the midbrain to the limbic system and prefrontal cortex.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","sourcePrintedPage":487,"sourcePdfPage":505},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to the glutamate hypothesis of schizophrenia , schizophrenia results at least in part from a dysfunction of glutamate transmission.","headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","sourcePrintedPage":488,"sourcePdfPage":506}],"topicIds":["bp14-m14-3-h01","bp14-m14-3-h02","bp14-m14-3-h03","bp14-m14-3-h04","bp14-m14-3-h05","bp14-m14-3-h06","bp14-m14-3-h07","bp14-m14-3-h08","bp14-m14-3-h09","bp14-m14-3-h10","bp14-m14-3-h11","bp14-m14-3-h12","bp14-m14-3-h13","bp14-m14-3-h14","bp14-m14-3-h15"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m14-3-study-1","title":"What schizophrenia means","text":"Schizophrenia is associated with disturbances in perception, beliefs, thinking, motivation, and social or occupational functioning. The term does not mean multiple personalities. Positive symptoms refer to experiences or behaviors added to typical functioning, such as hallucinations or delusions; negative symptoms refer to reductions in functions such as motivation or expressive behavior. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment and consideration of other possible causes. Biological measures are informative for research but are not simple stand-alone diagnostic tests.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":481,"sourcePrintedEnd":491,"sourcePdfStart":499,"sourcePdfEnd":509},{"id":"bp14-m14-3-study-2","title":"Genetic susceptibility and environment","text":"Family and adoption research supports a genetic contribution to risk, but schizophrenia does not follow one straightforward Mendelian pattern. Many genetic variants and developmental influences are implicated, and having a predisposition does not mean the disorder will necessarily develop. Research considers prenatal and early-life factors, later stressors, and other environmental influences. Findings from group studies need careful interpretation because different people may arrive at similar clinical symptoms through partly different pathways.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":481,"sourcePrintedEnd":491,"sourcePdfStart":499,"sourcePdfEnd":509},{"id":"bp14-m14-3-study-3","title":"Brain findings and explanatory limits","text":"Studies report differences in certain brain structures, circuits, and aspects of neural function among groups, but these findings overlap with variation in the wider population. A structural difference does not by itself establish whether it contributed to the disorder, followed from illness, or relates to treatment or other factors. Researchers therefore combine anatomical, behavioral, and pharmacological evidence rather than claiming to have discovered one unique 'schizophrenia region'.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":481,"sourcePrintedEnd":491,"sourcePdfStart":499,"sourcePdfEnd":509},{"id":"bp14-m14-3-study-4","title":"Dopamine, glutamate, and treatment","text":"Many antipsychotic drugs influence dopamine receptors and can reduce particular symptoms, supporting a role for dopamine-related pathways. However, the dopamine account does not explain all features of schizophrenia. Glutamate-related processes and other signaling systems have also received attention. Newer treatments may differ in receptor action and adverse effects, but medication alone does not address every functional difficulty. A complete view includes symptom management, psychological and social support, and the limits of current mechanistic understanding.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":481,"sourcePrintedEnd":491,"sourcePdfStart":499,"sourcePdfEnd":509}],"contentLevel":"complete_sample_classroom_notes_plus_legacy_source_extraction","selfCheck":[{"question":"Can you explain: What schizophrenia means?","answer":"Schizophrenia is associated with disturbances in perception, beliefs, thinking, motivation, and social or occupational functioning. .","printedPage":482,"pdfPage":500,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":19},{"text":"In addition to the defining symptoms, researchers have reported .","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":29},{"text":"The high concordance for monozygotic twins has long been taken as .","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"Also note the greater similarity between dizygotic twins than between siblings in Figure 14.13.","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"Dizygotic twins have the same .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"The results vary from one study to another, partly because some also consistent with a prenatal influence.","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"When their children develop schizophrenia, we cannot be sure that the reason is genetic.","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":39},{"text":"A study of adopted children in Finland found a high probability of schizophrenia or related conditions among","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":40},{"text":"children who had a biological mother with schizophrenia and a severely disordered adopting family.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":41},{"text":"A pregnant woman with schizophrenia passes her genes to her child, but she also provides the prenatal environment.","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":119},{"text":"Many women with schizophrenia abuse alcohol or other drugs, eat a poor diet, and have complications during pregnancy and delivery.","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":120},{"text":"The genetic risk itself or the disordered family itself had less effect, as shown in Figure 14.14.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":121}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":191,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":180},{"id":"bp14-m14-3-h06","title":"Identified average between people with or without schizophrenia, including many that code for proteins in the brain .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"The results vary from one study to another, partly because some genes are common in one ethnic group but not in another .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"No common genetic variant produces more than a small increase in the probability of schizophrenia.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"A few rare genes are known to greatly increase the risk of schizophrenia, mostly by disrupting the development of glutamate synapses or by interfering with the immune system .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Certain genes are described as “intolerant of loss of function.” Geneticists only occasionally find variants in those genes because the variants decrease survival or reproduction.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":47},{"text":"The common genes producing a small risk and the rare genes causing a greater risk mostly affect the same brain functions, just to different degrees .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"Even a tiny deletion of a critical segment can lead to cognitive dysfunction and symptoms of schizophrenia .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"Indeed, it would be difficult for any gene with a strong link to schizophrenia to become common, because people with schizophrenia have, on average, fewer than half as many children as other people do, and their brothers and sisters do not compensate by having more children than average.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":122},{"text":"One common gene related to schizophrenia alters the major histocompatibility complex—that is, genes controlling cell surface proteins that the immune system recognizes.","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":123},{"text":"Another important gene, called DISC1 (disrupted in .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":51},{"text":"The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, an area often impaired in .","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"Presumably, the effects of brain damage were minimal at age 1 year .","printedPage":485,"pdfPage":503,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"The risk also increases if the mother was exposed to extreme stress, .","printedPage":488,"pdfPage":506,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":100},{"text":"Ordinarily, those NMDA receptors stimulate neurons that inhibit .","printedPage":489,"pdfPage":507,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":105},{"text":"One reason is that many patients do not get the treatments that are is a clinical syndrome involving disturbances of thought, perception, motivation and functioning. It should not be confused with alternating personalities. The textbook stresses variability across people.","paragraphIndex":20000,"bullets":[{"label":"Positive symptoms","explanation":"Hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech or behavior are experiences or actions added to usual functioning.","paragraphIndex":20001},{"label":"Negative and cognitive symptoms","explanation":"Reduced expression, initiative or social engagement, together with difficulties in attention and memory, can create major disability even when conspicuous positive symptoms are controlled.","paragraphIndex":20002},{"label":"Positive and negative symptoms","explanation":"Positive symptoms add unusual experiences or behaviors, such as hallucinations and delusions; negative symptoms involve reductions in motivation, emotional expression, or ordinary engagement.","paragraphIndex":78300},{"label":"Diagnosis requires context","explanation":"Disorganized thought or unusual beliefs must be understood alongside other symptoms and medical and cultural considerations.","paragraphIndex":78301}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Schizophrenia involves disturbances in thought, perception, emotion, and motivation, but it does not mean having multiple personalities. Diagnosis relies on a pattern of symptoms, their duration, and resulting impairment.","followUpParagraphIndex":53400,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h02","title":"Differential Diagnosis of Schizophrenia","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h01","printedPage":482,"pdfPage":500,"explanation":"A schizophrenia diagnosis requires more than recognizing one unusual belief or a report of hearing a voice. Clinicians must evaluate persistence, functional change and possible alternative explanations.","paragraphIndex":20003,"bullets":[{"label":"Differential process","explanation":"Mood disorders, medical illness, substance effects and other conditions can produce overlapping symptoms and require separate assessment.","paragraphIndex":20004},{"label":"Heterogeneity","explanation":"Two people receiving the same diagnosis may share relatively few symptoms or biological findings; the label may cover a family of related pathways.","paragraphIndex":20005},{"label":"Rule out alternatives","explanation":"Substances, other psychiatric illnesses, neurological conditions, and certain medical problems may produce psychotic or cognitive symptoms.","paragraphIndex":78302},{"label":"Why important","explanation":"A symptom list alone cannot establish cause. Correct interpretation influences both scientific conclusions and clinical care.","paragraphIndex":78303}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"A differential diagnosis asks what other condition might better account for symptoms resembling schizophrenia. Similar manifestations can arise for different reasons.","followUpParagraphIndex":53401,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","title":"Genetic Influences","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"explanation":"Genetic factors contribute substantially to susceptibility, but the pattern is complex. Risk is distributed among many variants and interacts with developmental conditions.","paragraphIndex":20006,"bullets":[{"label":"Inheritance","explanation":"Greater biological relatedness is associated with higher average risk; it is a probability, not destiny.","paragraphIndex":20007},{"label":"Limits","explanation":"Even very close relatives can differ, showing that genetic similarity does not guarantee a shared clinical outcome.","paragraphIndex":20008},{"label":"Many small contributions","explanation":"Modern genetic evidence points to numerous variants, often affecting broader developmental or neural pathways.","paragraphIndex":78304},{"label":"Probabilistic risk","explanation":"Even identical twins are not perfectly concordant, showing that genetic similarity does not eliminate environmental and developmental influences.","paragraphIndex":78305}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Family and twin studies provide strong evidence that inherited variation influences schizophrenia risk, but no single common gene determines who develops it.","followUpParagraphIndex":53402,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h04","title":"Family Studies","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"explanation":"Family studies compare schizophrenia rates across relatives to estimate familial clustering. They help raise genetic hypotheses but cannot by themselves rule out shared experience.","paragraphIndex":20009,"bullets":[{"label":"Useful comparison","explanation":"Risk tends to increase with genetic relatedness, which is compatible with inherited vulnerability.","paragraphIndex":20010},{"label":"Caution","explanation":"Relatives often share environments, so adoption, twin and molecular approaches are needed to clarify what the observed similarity means.","paragraphIndex":20011},{"label":"Concordance","explanation":"When one identical twin has schizophrenia, the other has higher risk than a fraternal co-twin, but is not certain to develop the condition.","paragraphIndex":78306},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"Sharing genes and sharing an environment are not completely separable in every family design; agreement rates support genetic influence without proving genetic inevitability.","paragraphIndex":78307}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Comparing twins and families helps separate some inherited contributions from shared living conditions. Greater resemblance between identical than fraternal twins is important evidence.","followUpParagraphIndex":53403,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h05","title":"Adopted Children Who Develop Schizophrenia","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","printedPage":483,"pdfPage":501,"explanation":"Adoption research separates some genetic relationships from the family environment in which a child grows up. It provides one way to examine inherited vulnerability and stressful contexts together.","paragraphIndex":20012,"bullets":[{"label":"Main logic","explanation":"A child can share genes with biological parents but much of the home environment with adoptive parents.","paragraphIndex":20013},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"Findings support an inherited component while also suggesting that adverse environments can matter particularly when vulnerability is already elevated.","paragraphIndex":20014},{"label":"Typical finding","explanation":"Schizophrenia occurs more often in biological relatives of affected adoptees than in their adoptive relatives in the studies discussed.","paragraphIndex":78308},{"label":"What it means","explanation":"Genetic influence is supported, while prenatal environment and how adoption placements differ must still be considered. Adoption does not remove every environmental influence.","paragraphIndex":78309}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Adoption studies examine whether risk follows biological kinship when a child grows up in another family. They complement twin studies but also have methodological limitations.","followUpParagraphIndex":53404,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h06","title":"Identified Genes","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h03","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"explanation":"Molecular studies identify many genetic associations rather than a single causative schizophrenia gene. Individual variations generally explain only a small portion of risk.","paragraphIndex":20015,"bullets":[{"label":"Genetic complexity","explanation":"Many associated variants influence neural development or functioning, and different people may carry different combinations.","paragraphIndex":20016},{"label":"Translation challenge","explanation":"A statistical association cannot directly diagnose schizophrenia or identify a universally effective therapy.","paragraphIndex":20017},{"label":"Polygenic pattern","explanation":"Small average effects can accumulate and overlap with risk for other psychiatric conditions.","paragraphIndex":78310},{"label":"Caution","explanation":"Identified associations vary across ancestry groups and research samples. Genetic studies are useful for understanding biological pathways but do not yet allow reliable individual prediction.","paragraphIndex":78311}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Large genetic studies identify many loci associated with schizophrenia, rather than one decisive mutation found in everyone with the disorder.","followUpParagraphIndex":53405,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","title":"Environmental Influences","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"explanation":"Environmental influences are especially relevant when considering when symptoms first appear and why genetically susceptible individuals do not all develop the disorder.","paragraphIndex":20018,"bullets":[{"label":"Timing","explanation":"Prenatal, early-life and later-life experiences may affect neural development and stress systems at different stages.","paragraphIndex":20019},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"A risk factor changes group probability; it is not evidence that a particular person or caregiver caused an illness.","paragraphIndex":20020},{"label":"Timing","explanation":"Some relevant brain regions, including prefrontal systems, develop slowly and take on new functions during adolescence and early adulthood.","paragraphIndex":78312},{"label":"Multiple-hit idea","explanation":"Inherited vulnerability and environmental events at different stages can interact. The hypothesis does not imply every affected person has the same combination of exposures.","paragraphIndex":78313}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Neurodevelopmental accounts propose that earlier influences may change the developing brain in ways that become visible much later. Schizophrenia does not necessarily begin biologically when symptoms first appear.","followUpParagraphIndex":53406,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h08","title":"Prenatal or Early Postnatal Factors","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","printedPage":484,"pdfPage":502,"explanation":"Early developmental factors can alter later vulnerability even when symptoms do not become evident until adolescence or adulthood. The textbook considers prenatal and early postnatal influences.","paragraphIndex":20021,"bullets":[{"label":"Possible pathways","explanation":"Maternal infection, inflammation and developmental disruptions are investigated because they can affect the developing nervous system.","paragraphIndex":20022},{"label":"Research limit","explanation":"Epidemiological associations must be checked for other explanations; they should not be treated as specific prenatal diagnoses.","paragraphIndex":20023},{"label":"Possible contributors","explanation":"Problems in nutrition, birth circumstances, and certain maternal infections have been investigated as risk factors.","paragraphIndex":78314},{"label":"Strength of evidence","explanation":"Most individual associations are small and do not imply that a common pregnancy complication will lead to psychosis. Correlation can reflect more than one causal pathway.","paragraphIndex":78315}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"The text reviews prenatal and early postnatal circumstances that are statistically associated with later schizophrenia, such as complications affecting early development.","followUpParagraphIndex":53407,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h09","title":"Factors Later in Life","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h07","printedPage":485,"pdfPage":503,"explanation":"Experiences later in life may contribute to the timing and severity of symptoms in a person who already has some vulnerability.","paragraphIndex":20024,"bullets":[{"label":"Stress and context","explanation":"Adversity and other life circumstances may add risk or make an episode harder to manage.","paragraphIndex":20025},{"label":"No simple cause","explanation":"A single stressful event does not define schizophrenia; inherited, developmental and environmental pathways can combine in many patterns.","paragraphIndex":20026},{"label":"Stress physiology","explanation":"Adversity can alter stress-response systems, which may interact with neurodevelopmental vulnerability.","paragraphIndex":78316},{"label":"Complex findings","explanation":"The book discusses additional correlations, including infections and migration-related experiences. None is a universal cause; researchers must examine confounding influences and the direction of effects.","paragraphIndex":78317}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Later experiences also matter, including prolonged stress and some traumatic childhood experiences. Their effects depend on a person's biological susceptibility and other environmental conditions.","followUpParagraphIndex":53408,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h10","title":"Brain Abnormalities","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":485,"pdfPage":503,"explanation":"Researchers have reported average differences in brain anatomy and function in groups diagnosed with schizophrenia. No one brain-scan pattern uniquely identifies every patient.","paragraphIndex":20027,"bullets":[{"label":"Network differences","explanation":"Changes in cortical or ventricular measures and in functional connections can correlate with illness characteristics.","paragraphIndex":20028},{"label":"Careful inference","explanation":"Brain abnormalities may precede illness, emerge with it or be affected by later experiences and treatment; an observed difference does not establish causation.","paragraphIndex":20029},{"label":"Patterns reported","explanation":"The text discusses gray- and white-matter differences and, in some samples, enlarged ventricles or changes involving prefrontal and hippocampal areas.","paragraphIndex":78318},{"label":"Avoid overclaiming","explanation":"A group-average difference is not a diagnostic scan. Medication exposure, other health factors, and differences among individuals complicate interpretation.","paragraphIndex":78319}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Brain imaging and anatomical studies find average group differences in some people with schizophrenia, but these findings vary and overlap extensively with observations in unaffected people.","followUpParagraphIndex":53409,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","title":"Treatments","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":486,"pdfPage":504,"explanation":"Treatment seeks to reduce distress and disability, especially disruptive positive symptoms, while supporting day-to-day life. Different symptom domains respond differently.","paragraphIndex":20030,"bullets":[{"label":"Medications","explanation":"Antipsychotic agents are especially relevant to hallucinations and delusions; treatment response and side effects vary.","paragraphIndex":20031},{"label":"Broader care","explanation":"Psychological, social and functional support remains important because medication alone often does not fully address negative or cognitive symptoms.","paragraphIndex":20032},{"label":"What can improve","explanation":"Many medications reduce certain positive symptoms, while difficulties with motivation, cognition, and community functioning may persist.","paragraphIndex":78320},{"label":"Outcome questions","explanation":"Side effects, continuity of care, early support, and access to services all influence results. A narrow measure of reduced hallucinations does not capture the entire person's recovery.","paragraphIndex":78321}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Treatment includes antipsychotic medication and broader psychological and social support. Managing symptoms is not identical to restoring every aspect of cognition or day-to-day functioning.","followUpParagraphIndex":53410,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h12","title":"Antipsychotic Drugs and Dopamine","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","printedPage":486,"pdfPage":504,"explanation":"Many antipsychotic drugs affect dopamine receptors, providing evidence that dopamine pathways contribute to some symptoms. It does not follow that the disorder is simply too much dopamine everywhere.","paragraphIndex":20033,"bullets":[{"label":"Mechanism","explanation":"Dopamine D2 receptor blockade is important for the effects of many standard antipsychotics.","paragraphIndex":20034},{"label":"Limits","explanation":"Positive symptoms commonly improve more than negative and cognitive symptoms; blocking dopamine can also cause movement or other unwanted effects.","paragraphIndex":20035},{"label":"Receptor evidence","explanation":"Drugs that block dopamine D2 receptors tend to reduce some psychotic symptoms, and their receptor-binding properties are relevant to effective doses.","paragraphIndex":78322},{"label":"Limitations","explanation":"Dopamine activity varies across pathways; not all symptoms respond equally, and treatment can produce movement-related side effects.","paragraphIndex":78323}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"The dopamine hypothesis gained support from the relationship between antipsychotic drug effectiveness and dopamine-receptor blockade. It is evidence for a pathway, not proof that all schizophrenia results from too much dopamine everywhere.","followUpParagraphIndex":53411,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h13","title":"Newer Antipsychotic Drugs","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","printedPage":487,"pdfPage":505,"explanation":"Newer antipsychotic treatments act on several receptor systems and may have different adverse-effect profiles. “Newer” does not mean uniformly better for every person.","paragraphIndex":20036,"bullets":[{"label":"Receptor diversity","explanation":"Some medications alter serotonin as well as dopamine signaling, changing both therapeutic and unwanted effects.","paragraphIndex":20037},{"label":"Clinical comparison","explanation":"Researchers evaluate symptom reduction, relapse prevention and burdens such as movement or metabolic effects rather than relying only on age of the drug.","paragraphIndex":20038},{"label":"Different receptor profiles","explanation":"Some newer agents influence dopamine and serotonin systems differently from older antipsychotics.","paragraphIndex":78324},{"label":"Trade-offs","explanation":"Movement symptoms, metabolic problems, subjective wellbeing, and response vary by treatment. The textbook warns that manufacturer-sponsored comparisons can bias the impression of superiority.","paragraphIndex":78325}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Newer antipsychotics interact with multiple signaling systems and were developed partly to improve tolerability and symptom control. They are not uniformly superior on every outcome.","followUpParagraphIndex":53412,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-3-h14","title":"Role of Glutamate","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-3-h11","printedPage":488,"pdfPage":506,"explanation":"Glutamate is another proposed contributor because it supports excitation, learning and neural circuit regulation. This broadens schizophrenia research beyond dopamine alone.","paragraphIndex":20039,"bullets":[{"label":"Hypothesis","explanation":"Interference with NMDA-type glutamate receptor activity can produce some schizophrenia-like experiences or cognitive disturbances.","paragraphIndex":20040},{"label":"Open question","explanation":"Evidence implicating glutamate does not yet provide a complete causal theory or a single successful treatment for all symptoms.","paragraphIndex":20041},{"label":"NMDA mechanism","explanation":"Reduced activity at certain glutamate receptors can disrupt the balance of excitation and inhibition in cortical circuits.","paragraphIndex":78326},{"label":"Not a final explanation","explanation":"The drug-model finding suggests a pathway worth studying; it does not establish that one glutamate abnormality explains every presentation or supplies a universally effective treatment.","paragraphIndex":78327}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Glutamate hypotheses arose partly from the observation that substances interfering with NMDA-type glutamate signaling can produce schizophrenia-like symptoms. The effects need not look like the same change at every synapse.","paragraphIndex":800782},{"label":"Connection to dopamine","explanation":"Glutamate and dopamine systems interact. A change in one can influence the activity of another, so apparent evidence for one system does not eliminate the other.","paragraphIndex":800783},{"label":"What remains uncertain","explanation":"The disorder is heterogeneous, the evidence does not point to one pathway in every patient, and a convincing mechanism must eventually explain symptoms and useful clinical outcomes.","paragraphIndex":800784}],"explanation":"Glutamate hypotheses of schizophrenia investigate how altered excitatory signaling, particularly at NMDA-type receptors, could contribute to symptoms and circuit dysfunction. Individual variations generally explain only a small portion of risk.","Many associated variants influence neural development or functioning, and different people may carry different combinations.","A statistical association cannot directly diagnose schizophrenia or identify a universally effective therapy.","Environmental influences are especially relevant when considering when symptoms first appear and why genetically susceptible individuals do not all develop the disorder.","Prenatal, early-life and later-life experiences may affect neural development and stress systems at different stages.","A risk factor changes group probability; it is not evidence that a particular person or caregiver caused an illness.","Early developmental factors can alter later vulnerability even when symptoms do not become evident until adolescence or adulthood. The textbook considers prenatal and early postnatal influences.","Maternal infection, inflammation and developmental disruptions are investigated because they can affect the developing nervous system.","Epidemiological associations must be checked for other explanations; they should not be treated as specific prenatal diagnoses.","Experiences later in life may contribute to the timing and severity of symptoms in a person who already has some vulnerability.","Adversity and other life circumstances may add risk or make an episode harder to manage.","A single stressful event does not define schizophrenia; inherited, developmental and environmental pathways can combine in many patterns.","Researchers have reported average differences in brain anatomy and function in groups diagnosed with schizophrenia. No one brain-scan pattern uniquely identifies every patient.","Changes in cortical or ventricular measures and in functional connections can correlate with illness characteristics.","Brain abnormalities may precede illness, emerge with it or be affected by later experiences and treatment; an observed difference does not establish causation.","Treatment seeks to reduce distress and disability, especially disruptive positive symptoms, while supporting day-to-day life. Different symptom domains respond differently.","Antipsychotic agents are especially relevant to hallucinations and delusions; treatment response and side effects vary.","Psychological, social and functional support remains important because medication alone often does not fully address negative or cognitive symptoms.","Many antipsychotic drugs affect dopamine receptors, providing evidence that dopamine pathways contribute to some symptoms. It does not follow that the disorder is simply too much dopamine everywhere.","Dopamine D2 receptor blockade is important for the effects of many standard antipsychotics.","Positive symptoms commonly improve more than negative and cognitive symptoms; blocking dopamine can also cause movement or other unwanted effects.","Newer antipsychotic treatments act on several receptor systems and may have different adverse-effect profiles. “Newer” does not mean uniformly better for every person.","Some medications alter serotonin as well as dopamine signaling, changing both therapeutic and unwanted effects.","Researchers evaluate symptom reduction, relapse prevention and burdens such as movement or metabolic effects rather than relying only on age of the drug.","Glutamate is another proposed contributor because it supports excitation, learning and neural circuit regulation. This broadens schizophrenia research beyond dopamine alone.","Interference with NMDA-type glutamate receptor activity can produce some schizophrenia-like experiences or cognitive disturbances.","Evidence implicating glutamate does not yet provide a complete causal theory or a single successful treatment for all symptoms.","The final message is uncertainty with progress: multiple routes can produce overlapping symptoms, and available treatments only partly address the range of impairments.","A useful explanation relates development, genes, networks, neurotransmitters and environment rather than treating any one as sufficient.","Ask separately what evidence concerns diagnosis, what concerns increased risk, and what actually demonstrates an effective treatment."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Essential reasoning: multiple pathways, partial drug response","body":"Family and adoption research support inherited susceptibility, while neurodevelopmental and environmental studies identify other contributions.
